F-log-watermark.rationale: The Fact's validity_context now states the two confirmed runtime violations of the condition as the actual established meaning of the claim, and the second unknown is narrowed to the variant that remains open. The leader-side trace behind the narrowing: replicateTo lowers nextIndex with max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1) using the follower's stale LastLog, so it is clamped above the follower's real log end; setupAppendEntries sets PrevLogEntry=0 once nextIndex reaches 1 and setNewLogs reads the leader's own store, so an error - and therefore the SEND_SNAP fallback - only occurs when the leader's log is missing an index. With the leader still holding the log, every attempt therefore fails on the follower's deleted index and nextIndex converges to 1, so no snapshot is sent and the follower stays divergent short of a restart.

feedback.answered: The boundary left open by the confirmed truncation-failure finding is answered for the case where the leader still holds the log: the follower cannot be resynchronized. Its stale LastLog is what the leader uses to lower nextIndex (replication.go 258-263), so nextIndex is clamped above the follower's real log end; the leader then walks it down one index at a time, every attempt is rejected by the follower at the index it no longer holds, and because setupAppendEntries only returns ErrLogNotFound when the leader's own store lacks an index (setPreviousLog short-circuits at nextIndex==1, setNewLogs reads the leader's log), the SEND_SNAP fallback is never reached. The follower therefore stays a divergent voter until it restarts, which rebuilds the watermark from durable state.
